Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the respondents submitted that 3rd (Ka) schedule land was recorded in the name of Alam Khan in CR Khatian, Defendant No. 3 contends the (Ka) schedule land was acquired by Alam Khan before CR operation and that his name was duly correctly recorded in CR Khatian. The plaintiff stated that Alam Khan has no title and possession in (Ka) and (Kha) schedules land and Bahadur Khan acquired (Ka) and (Kha) schedule land with his money in the benami of his son Alam Khan Both the Courts below concurrently held relying on evidence that this land was purchased in the benami of Alam Khan and the plaintiff had share in it. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that the transfer of Asma on 18-2-1918 to defendant No. 3 father of Alep Khan has been found valid by the trial Court but the appellate Court without any cogent ground overturned referred the same. 

 12. The learned Counsel for the respondent argued that 3rd (Ka) schedule land was recorded in the name of Alam Khan in CS Khatian. Defendant No. 3 contends that 'Ka' schedule land was acquired by Alam Khan before CS operation and that his name was duly and correctly recorded in CS Khatian. The plaintiff stated that Alam Khan had no title possession in 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedules land and Bahadur Khan acquired 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedules land with his own money in the benami of his son Alam Khan. Both the Courts below concurrently held relying on evidence that land was purchased in the benami of Alam Khan and the plaintiff had share in it. The Advocate further submitted that the transfer of Asma on 18-2-1918 to defendant No. 3, father Alep Khan has been found valid by the trial Court but the Court of Appeal below without any cogent ground set aside the same.
